Hi Elena — thanks again for carving out time earlier. Short recap from our side plus clear next steps so your team (and ours) has a single source of truth.

Quick TL;DR
- Primary goal: replace current on-prem keyword extraction and reranking service with an LLM-powered scoring layer by Q2 2027.
- Hard SLOs: p95 latency <= 220ms for inline scoring (128 token avg); throughput target 1.5k reqs/min sustained with 3x burst headroom.
- Model preference: start with a quantized 8-bit LLM (Llama2-family variant you already validated) with ability to failover to a smaller, cheaper variant for non-critical traffic.
- Deployment: Dedicated Redwood pool in us-west with private peering to ArsenalTX VPC; KV prefix caching and warmup windows required.

What we heard (pain points)
- Current system struggles when traffic spikes (Black Friday-like bursts); autoscaling churn causes cold starts and lost requests.
- Operator overhead: manual model swaps and opaque latency spikes.
- Cost strain: token-based jobs driving unpredictable bills.

Technical constraints you called out
- All inference must remain within your VPC (no model weights leave the environment).
- SOC2 + PCI adjacent; audit logs required for every inference route.
- 2-week notice for any maintenance that impacts model versions in production.

Our proposed fit (high level)
- Redwood Private (dedicated deployment inside ArsenalTX VPC) with a private control plane and customer-managed KMS.
- Autoscaling policy: combination of concurrency-based scaling and a pre-warmed burst pool sized to 3x observed peak QPS.
- KV/PREFIX cache: recommend 48-hour TTL for common prefixes; use continuous batching for bulk scorer endpoints.
- Fallbacks: routing policy that demotes to a quantized-small variant during capacity shortages; probabilistic sample of outputs sent to the larger model for quality monitoring.

Immediate action items (owner / ETA)
1) ArsenalTX: share recent 7-day traffic histograms (per route) + representative sample prompts — Elena / techops — by 2026-11-24. (needed for sizing + batching simulator)
2) Redwood: deliver an SLO-fit spreadsheet (includes cost model, burst sizing, KV cache config) — Vivek — by 2026-11-24. (attached draft)
3) Technical deep-dive call with your infra + security teams — 60m — target week of 2026-11-30 — Mina to coordinate.
4) Draft contract notes for Private deployment (data residency & KMS clause) — Connor — draft ready by 2026-12-02.

Attachments: redwood-slo-summary-v1.pdf (SLO assumptions + cost simulation), kv-cache-proposal.xlsx (batching & cache parameters).

Next proposed meeting
- 60-minute technical deep-dive (infra + security + dev leads). Proposed slots: Tue 2026-11-30 09:00-10:00 PT or Wed 2026-12-01 11:00-12:00 PT. Please confirm which works.

If anything above doesn't match your notes, flag it and we'll correct. Otherwise we'll treat this as the canonical post-call readout and follow the action item owners/timelines above.
